scope: Existing exact-source source and two four-block raw result files inspected; no benchmark/build/source edits. Original first-block negative evidence preserved.
decision: HOLD Aff main merge. Do not rename unresolved perf risk as structural cleanup acceptance. Stop additional full wall-time matrices now; release main resource window for the already pending MC/output-pieces composition acceptance.
why: Every one of272 new rows is valid; all original nine requests present in both modes. Semantic acceptance is intact.

Repeated native private is slower in3/4 pairs: ratios1.152,1.339,0.836,1.104; GM1.092 and CPU GM1.090. Including retained first run gives4/5 negative private pairs; this is a risk signal, not proof of algorithmic regression or a statistically established9% true effect.

Check private is also slower in3/4 pairs; its GM0.958 is reversed by one baseline1149ms/candidate465ms pair. Therefore the favorable GM cannot establish nonregression. Check unchanged3/4 slower, GM1.117, while native unchanged3/4 faster with a candidate1065ms outlier.

Native multi and several other scenarios improved in this window; broad is near equal. This contradicts a uniform global slowdown but does not resolve the targeted private-edit risk. CPU and wall ratios broadly agree, so a pure waiting-only explanation is insufficient.

Actual removal of temporary all-CFG publication clone and repeated unchanged fragment serialization is source-proven, but that structural reduction alone cannot guarantee whole-request improvement. User goal is actual speed, and no required nonregression threshold has been demonstrated.

environment.interpretation: Five allowed logical CPUs under four-CPU quota, not a fixed-core experiment. This permits environmental variation, but cannot by itself attribute the observed differences to scheduler noise. No claim that CPU quota was saturated during the runs.

one_bounded_next_diagnostic.priority: Only if root allocates a small diagnostic slot after the pending composition work; do not block that work or run more full matrices.
one_bounded_next_diagnostic.method: Use existing release IR/base rlibs to build identical small ordinary-codec harnesses, one per arm, on the same validated actual5.3MB function-wire fixture. Decode outside the encoder timing, ensure both output bytes match the original exactly, use black_box and retain a checksum to prevent elision, and include output allocation/destruction in each encode iteration. Alternate bounded batches on the same explicitly chosen allowed CPU for both harnesses. This requires root execution authorization/window; not run by reviewer.
one_bounded_next_diagnostic.limits: A newly linked harness has a different call graph and may not reproduce final full-CLI ThinLTO inlining/layout. A harness result is localization evidence only, not full compiler acceptance, not no-op evidence, and not proof of a net main-stage gain. Do not benchmark a detached byte copy and call it compiler speed.
one_bounded_next_diagnostic.conditional_source_slice: If ordinary codec is repeatedly slower, restore Writer::module ordinary implementation to the baseline direct TypedFunction loop, leaving immutable product encoding behind its separate entry. Keep the owner cache, quota accounting, current headers and exact first-error behavior. Prefer that explicit isolation to blindly adding inline(always) across the large shared module function. Validate exact byte/limit oracles and the one changed publication/private path before any main decision.
one_bounded_next_diagnostic.exit: If ordinary codec is not slower, do not chase speculative Arc/group rewrites or endless repeats. Keep Aff available/archived as a semantically accepted but performance-unaccepted stage and proceed with the pending larger composition. Revisit with concrete phase evidence when that work supplies it.
